description: This bar chart, from the paper “2-Tier SimCSE Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings,” compares three performance metrics—Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue)—across five different model configurations: Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, and Supervised_SimCSE (the last two are grouped together under a single label on the x-axis). The vertical y-axis, labeled “Accuracy / Correlation,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 0.8, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 0.2, and the horizontal x-axis lists the model configurations in the order they appear. Each model configuration has three adjacent bars, one for each metric, with the bars grouped side-by-side. The “Single-task_baseline” model shows the lowest performance overall, with Sentiment Acc. at approximately 0.53, STS Corr. at approximately 0.50, and Paraphrase Acc. at approximately 0.79. The “Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout” model shows improved Sentiment Acc. (around 0.52) and STS Corr. (around 0.58), while Paraphrase Acc. remains high at approximately 0.78. The “Unsupervised_SimCSE” model further improves STS Corr. to approximately 0.70, while Sentiment Acc. and Paraphrase Acc. remain around 0.52 and 0.77, respectively. The “Supervised_SimCSE” model demonstrates the highest performance across all metrics, with STS Corr. reaching approximately 0.81, Paraphrase Acc. at approximately 0.78, and Sentiment Acc. at approximately 0.48. The bars are not sorted and are presented in the order of the model configurations as labeled on the x-axis. There is no visual emphasis such as shading, bolding, or outlining applied to any specific bar.
